decisionCount.note: THIS IS THE HEADLINE. 2,211 mechanical sites collapse to 298 distinct values. One value (#00e5a0) is 665 of the 1,111 hex literals — 60% of the largest metric is a SINGLE decision. Conversely 353 of the 1,216 palette-class occurrences are dark:-prefixed and therefore inert: they are deletions, not mappings. Sizing Phase 3 by the ratchet numbers overstates the decision work by roughly an order of magnitude and understates the review work, which scales with ROUTES, not with sites.

proposedTokens.kind: bare-channel duplicates of existing :root semantic tokens
proposedTokens.why: The bare-channel mechanism ALREADY EXISTS and is proven — globals.css lines 251-338 declare --c-primary-500 etc. as "236 253 245" triples and tailwind.theme.cjs wraps them as rgb(var(--c-…) / <alpha-value>). But it covers ONLY the 50-900 ramps and the eh-* namespace. None of the SEMANTIC tokens (--surface, --border, --error, --primary …) has a channel form, which is exactly why all 55 bg-[var(--x)]/NN declarations are discarded.
proposedTokens.unlocks: 55 currently-dead declarations, and 390 currently-WORKING opacity modifiers (177 on [#hex], 213 on palette classes) that would become dead the moment a naive codemod rewrote them to -[var(--token)]/NN.
proposedTokens.alsoNeeded: Register matching named colours in tailwind.config.js theme.extend.colors so authors write bg-surface/80, border-brand/30, bg-danger/10 instead of arbitrary values. Named > arbitrary here: an arbitrary var() can be mis-typed again, a named colour cannot.

proposedTokens.value: mirror theme/palette.js chartSeries: #1f4230 #b08a3e #d96a4c #2f6d6a #7a4a63 #6b7a3e #46618c #8c5a3c (already contrast- and separability-checked there)
proposedTokens.why: There is NO categorical token set in :root. The palette has exactly three brand hues and four status hues, and several surfaces need N DISTINGUISHABLE hues where the hue is an identity label, not a status: widget-type gradients (app/dashboard/widgets/page.tsx:283-291 maps weather→blue, rss→orange, social→pink, clock→purple, countdown→red, sheets→green), template category chips (components/templates/TemplateCard.tsx:28-33 retail/restaurant/corporate/education/healthcare/events), content tags (components/ContentTagger.tsx), layout zone colours (app/dashboard/layouts/). Flattening these to forest destroys the distinction the UI is carrying; mapping them to --success/--warning/--error asserts a status that does not exist.
proposedTokens.unlocks: approx. 120 palette-class sites that are categorical, not semantic (see classification.categorical).

proposedTokens.kind: NEW — text/icon colour for a brand or status FILL
proposedTokens.why: #061a21 appears 116 times, 91 of them as class:text — it is EH near-black used as the label ON a neon fill. There is no general "ink on a fill" token: .eh-btn-neon hardcodes var(--lw-on-forest) and .eh-btn-danger hardcodes the keyword `white` (globals.css:1189). text-white appears 117 times in JSX and is invisible to the ratchet. Without this token the codemod has to pick per site between --lw-on-forest, white, and --foreground, and will get some wrong — and on a white-label tenant fill, pure white may fail AA where --on-primary derived per tenant would not.
proposedTokens.note: For white-label, --on-primary should be derived the same way --brand-ink-light is (readableInk against the tenant --primary), not fixed. That is a small addition to applyCSSVariables, not a new mechanism.

proposedTokens.value: rgba(35, 38, 31, 0.5) / rgba(35, 38, 31, 0.7) — warm ink, not neutral black
proposedTokens.why: bg-black/50 and bg-black/70 are used as scrims over template thumbnails and content previews (32 bg-black sites). On the ivory substrate a neutral-black scrim reads cold against everything around it — the same reason theme/chartConfig.ts:84 deliberately uses rgba(35,38,31,0.05) rather than a grey for the tooltip cursor.
proposedTokens.unlocks: 28 bg-black sites (18 of them bg-black/50) plus from-black/70 and via-white/20 gradient stops. NOTE: bg-black/50 WORKS today because black is a real Tailwind colour with channel support; rewriting it to bg-[var(--scrim)]/50 would kill it. --scrim must therefore carry its own alpha (like --surface-glass and --c-eh-card do) OR be registered as a channel-backed named colour.

proposedTokens.kind: NEW — the one legitimately dark panel
proposedTokens.why: admin/support paints bg-[#1F2937] (17 sites) / bg-[#374151] (4) / bg-[#111827] (3) — a dark slate panel — and then puts text-[var(--foreground-secondary)] (#4b5045, a DARK warm grey) on it. After Phase 1 that pairing is roughly 1.4:1. Either the panel becomes a light surface (then the token is --surface-secondary and no new token is needed) or it stays a deliberate dark panel and needs an inverse pair. This is a DESIGN DECISION, not a mapping — flagged, not decided.

deadOpacityDeclarations.explanation: bg-[var(--x)]/80 emits nothing: Tailwind can only build rgb(<channels> / .8), and rgb(#fdfbf5 / .8) is invalid CSS so the declaration is discarded. These elements have had NO background / border since they were written.
deadOpacityDeclarations.bareChannelPrecedent: globals.css:251-338 declares --c-primary-500: 236 253 245 etc. as bare channels, and tailwind.theme.cjs wraps every one as rgb(var(--c-…) / <alpha-value>). It covers the 50-900 ramps and the eh-* namespace ONLY. Extending the same mechanism to the semantic tokens is the fix; no new technique is needed. The one documented exception is --c-eh-card, which carries its own alpha and so cannot be a triple.

atRiskOpacityModifiers.explanation: These WORK today and would be silently destroyed by a naive rewrite to -[var(--token)]/NN. They are 7x the size of the existing bug and are the main reason the codemod must emit NAMED channel-backed colours rather than arbitrary var() values.

list.name: A component class declared after @tailwind utilities beats the utility
list.status: LIVE — 133 elements, 238 colour utilities at risk, 35 files
list.evidence: web/src/app/globals.css:3 is `@tailwind utilities;`. Every .eh-*, .lw-* and .mkt-* rule is declared at top level from line 480 onward, i.e. AFTER it. Both are single-class selectors, so source order decides and the component class wins. 87 of those rules paint colour (verified by parsing the file). Worked example: app/dashboard/content/page-client.tsx:1693 and :1815 put text-amber-400 on an element that also carries .eh-icon-btn, which sets `color: var(--foreground-secondary)` at globals.css:1414 — the amber has never rendered.
list.forTheCodemod: Before rewriting a colour utility, check whether the same className carries an .eh-*/.lw-*/.mkt- class that sets the same property. If it does, the rewrite is a NO-OP and must be reported as such, not counted as progress. The list is in traps.componentClassOverride.

list.name: Inline style silently kills class-based hover:/focus: variants
list.evidence: Searched every `style={{ … color|backgroundColor|borderColor … }}` (49 sites) for a hover/focus/active/group-hover colour variant within the same JSX element window. Zero hits. The 49 inline colour styles are concentrated in charts (recharts needs them), widgets and the display renderer (both frozen), the white-label customization preview (the colour IS the data) and global-error.tsx.
list.forTheCodemod: Keep the check in the codemod as a guard — it costs nothing and the count is currently zero, which makes it a clean negative control. But do not spend review time on it.

list.name: font-[var(--x)] parses as font-WEIGHT and is dropped
list.status: NOT LIVE — 0 sites found; already fixed and fenced
list.evidence: Zero `font-[var(--…)]` in web/src. tailwind.config.js:36-40 now declares named fontFamily utilities (font-sora, font-dm, font-mono) specifically so nobody reaches for the arbitrary form again, and the config comment records the 35 call sites that were broken.
list.forTheCodemod: Never emit font-[var(…)]. If a font token is needed, emit the named utility.

list.name: Tailwind scans comments, so a hex in a comment regenerates the rule (and the ratchet counts it)
list.status: LIVE but benign — 28 hexes across 19 comment lines in 9 files
list.evidence: components/banner-tones.ts carries 12 (a computed contrast table), app/dashboard/layout.tsx 2, plus singles in ScheduleCalendar/Toast/Badge/EmergencyOverrideModal/TrialBanner/status-badge. Most are the CORRECT Little Worlds values recorded as contrast evidence.
list.forTheCodemod: Never rewrite a hex inside a comment. Deleting these to lower the ratchet would delete the computed-contrast evidence the redesign plan requires (plan §5: "never hand-asserted"). The ratchet floor is therefore NOT zero — it is roughly 40 (28 comment hexes + ~12 non-colour matches, see classification.notAColour).

list.name: THE BIG ONE — an opacity modifier on an arbitrary var() emits nothing
list.status: LIVE today at 55 sites; 390 more would be created by a naive codemod
list.evidence: Tailwind expands bg-x/80 to `rgb(<value> / .8)`. `rgb(#fdfbf5 / .8)` is invalid CSS and the whole declaration is dropped. The repo already knows this (tailwind.theme.cjs header, globals.css:236-241) and solved it for the 50-900 ramps with bare channels — but not for the semantic tokens. Today: 55 dead sites / 19 files. At risk: 177 opacity modifiers on [#hex] and 213 on palette classes, ALL of which work right now and would go dark the instant they became -[var(--token)]/NN.
list.forTheCodemod: HARD GATE. The codemod must refuse to emit `-[var(--x)]/NN` at all. Any source site carrying an opacity modifier must be rewritten to a NAMED, channel-backed colour (bg-brand/10) — which means B0 must land first and the codemod must fail loudly if the named colour it needs does not exist.

list.name: The Tailwind named colours still resolve to Electric Horizon values
list.status: LIVE — 24 sites, and invisible to the ratchet
list.evidence: theme/palette.js still holds the EH palette (its own header says so: "VALUES IN THIS FILE ARE THE ELECTRIC HORIZON PALETTE AND ARE NOT THE REDESIGN TARGET"). globals.css:252-263 therefore declares --c-primary-500: 0 229 160 — neon. So bg-primary-500 / text-primary-600 / bg-neutral-800 / bg-eh-surface render EH colours TODAY. The ratchet regex does not include `primary`, `eh` or the named `neutral`, so none of these is counted as debt. Measured: 24 primary-*/neutral-*/eh-* sites (11 of them in app/dashboard/page-client.tsx), plus 139 success/warning/error/info-NNN sites which happen to be close to correct.
list.forTheCodemod: Phase 3 must either (a) re-point palette.js to Little Worlds — which silently restyles all 163 sites at once with no diff to review — or (b) convert the 24 EH-valued sites to semantic tokens first and re-point afterwards. (b) is reviewable; (a) is not. Also: widen the ratchet regex to cover primary|eh|black|white, or these stay invisible.

list.name: black and white utilities are not counted at all
list.status: LIVE — 172 sites (45 of them carrying an opacity modifier)
list.evidence: Measured over the ratchet corpus (landing and tests excluded): text-white 111, bg-black/50 18, text-white/80 6, bg-white 6, border-white/10 4, border-white 3, bg-white/10 3, bg-black/70 3, bg-black 3, and a tail — 172 total, 45 of which carry an opacity modifier. The rawPaletteClasses regex lists 16 hue families and neither `black` nor `white`, so none of this is counted.
list.forTheCodemod: text-white on a forest fill should become --on-primary (PROPOSED) not stay white; bg-black scrims should become --scrim (PROPOSED). Widen the ratchet regex in the same PR that adds the tokens, and raise the baseline by 174 in that commit so the ratchet stays honest rather than appearing to regress.

widgetGalleryFallsThroughItsOwnTypeMap.whyTheRetractionLookedRight: There are TWO type lists in this one file and they disagree. DEFAULT_WIDGET_TYPES (page.tsx:17) holds weather, rss, social-feed, clock, sheets — and all five of those ARE in the map, so measuring against it returns a clean bill of health. But that constant is only reached through unavailableFallbackWidgetTypes() at page.tsx:255, i.e. ONLY when the types request throws, and it marks every entry available:false. On the normal path it contributes nothing but a name/description fallback. So the list that renders is the registry's, not this one. Anyone auditing this file top-down meets the wrong list first.
widgetGalleryFallsThroughItsOwnTypeMap.theSpellingTrap: The live social types are spelled with UNDERSCORES (social_instagram). A grep for the hyphenated `social-instagram` returns zero hits across the whole repo and reads as proof the types do not exist. They do: a DTO enum member (dto/create-widget.dto.ts:15-17) and a real data source each (social.data-source.ts:12,137,247). The rendered card titles are what misleads — page.tsx:236 derives a display name with `type.replace(/_/g,' ')`, which eats underscores but leaves hyphens, which is why the same row of cards shows `Social Instagram` (was social_instagram) next to `Generic-Api` (was generic-api). The visible name is not the key.

whichMapKeysAreActuallyDead.'social-media': DEAD. Zero occurrences anywhere outside this map — not in the registry, not in the DTO enum, not in DEFAULT_WIDGET_TYPES.
whichMapKeysAreActuallyDead.'social-feed' / 'clock' / 'sheets': NOT dead. Reachable through the API-unavailable fallback list, which still renders tiles.
whichMapKeysAreActuallyDead.'clock' / 'countdown': NOT dead for saved widgets either. Both are DTO enum members, so stored widgets can carry them and the My Widgets list (page.tsx:623,627) keys on widget.widgetType.
whichMapKeysAreActuallyDead.note: So the honest count is ONE dead key, not two, and 'countdown' is not one of them. Do not repeat the earlier 'two dead keys, one of which is only a mode of clock' framing — it was derived from the fallback list too.

widgetGalleryFallsThroughItsOwnTypeMap.whatThisIsNot: Not a colour bug and not fixable in a colour batch. The --cat-* values it reaches for are correct; the gap is that four product types have no assigned identity at all, and assigning them is a design decision about which hue means which platform. Logged here, deliberately not fixed.
widgetGalleryFallsThroughItsOwnTypeMap.ifSomeoneFixesIt: Key on the registry's spellings, not the gallery's labels, and fix getIconForType in the same change — it falls through for exactly the same four types, so a colour-only fix leaves four tiles still wearing one icon. The fallback itself is also worth a look: 'unknown type' currently renders as the brand gradient, which reads as a first-class category rather than an absence.
widgetGalleryFallsThroughItsOwnTypeMap.howThisGotMismeasuredTwice: Both readings were honest measurements of the wrong list. The durable rule: when a component has a constant that LOOKS like the domain enum, confirm which list actually reaches the render before treating either as ground truth — and prefer the rendered artefact, which cannot be fooled by picking the wrong constant.

Worked example: app/dashboard/content/page-client.tsx:1693 is className="eh-icon-btn text-amber-400", and globals.css:1414 sets .eh-icon-btn { color: var(--foreground-secondary) }. Both are single-class selectors, so source order decides and the component class wins — the amber has never rendered. Same at :1815.
trapsWithEvidence.forTheCodemod: Before rewriting a colour utility, check whether the same className carries an .eh-/.lw-/.mkt- class setting the same property. If it does, the rewrite is a NO-OP and must be REPORTED as one, not counted as progress. Full list at traps.componentClassOverride.

trapsWithEvidence.trap: Inline style silently kills class-based hover:/focus: variants
trapsWithEvidence.evidence: All 49 inline colour styles were checked for a hover/focus/active/group-hover colour variant in the same JSX element window. Zero hits. They are concentrated in charts (recharts requires them), components/widgets and app/display (both frozen), the white-label customization preview (the colour IS the data), and global-error.tsx.
trapsWithEvidence.forTheCodemod: Keep the check as a guard — it costs nothing and currently reads zero, which makes it a clean negative control. Do not spend review time on it.

trapsWithEvidence.trap: font-[var(--x)] is parsed as font-WEIGHT and the declaration is dropped
trapsWithEvidence.status: NOT LIVE — 0 sites, and already fenced
trapsWithEvidence.evidence: Zero font-[var(--…)] anywhere in web/src. tailwind.config.js:36-40 now declares named fontFamily utilities (font-sora, font-dm, font-mono) specifically so nobody reaches for the arbitrary form again, and the config comment records the 35 call sites that were broken by it. Tailwind's dataTypes.length rejects var(), so the colour-namespace inference that makes text-[var(--x)] safe does not apply here.
trapsWithEvidence.forTheCodemod: Never emit font-[var(…)]. If a font token is needed, emit the named utility.

trapsWithEvidence.trap: Tailwind scans comments, so a hex in a comment regenerates the rule — and the ratchet counts it
trapsWithEvidence.status: LIVE but benign — 28 hexes across 19 comment lines in 9 files
trapsWithEvidence.evidence: components/banner-tones.ts:6,44,45,46,47,48,51,52,56,57 (12 hexes — a computed contrast table); app/dashboard/layout.tsx:177,295; ScheduleCalendar.tsx:275; Toast.tsx:38; ui/Badge.tsx:77; fleet/EmergencyOverrideModal.tsx:210; TrialBanner.tsx:23,207; EntitlementBanner.tsx:32; settings/billing/components/status-badge.tsx:25.
trapsWithEvidence.forTheCodemod: NEVER rewrite a hex inside a comment. Most are the CORRECT Little Worlds values recorded as contrast evidence; deleting them to lower the ratchet deletes the evidence plan §5 requires. The ratchet header's advice — "prefer naming the token over quoting the hex" — governs NEW comments, it is not a mandate to strip existing ones.

trapsWithEvidence.trap: THE BIG ONE — an opacity modifier on an arbitrary var() emits nothing
trapsWithEvidence.status: LIVE at 55 sites today; 390 more would be CREATED by a naive codemod
trapsWithEvidence.evidence: Tailwind expands bg-x/80 to rgb(<value> / .8). rgb(#fdfbf5 / .8) is invalid CSS and the whole declaration is discarded. The repo already knows this — tailwind.theme.cjs header lines 16-27, globals.css:236-241 — and solved it for the 50-900 ramps with bare channels. It did NOT solve it for the semantic tokens, which is precisely why the 55 are dead. At risk: 177 opacity modifiers on [#hex], 213 on palette classes, 45 on black/white — all working right now.
trapsWithEvidence.forTheCodemod: HARD GATE. The codemod must REFUSE to emit -[var(--x)]/NN at all. Any source site carrying an opacity modifier must be rewritten to a NAMED, channel-backed colour (bg-brand/10). That means B0 lands first, and the codemod must FAIL LOUDLY if the named colour it needs does not exist rather than falling back to an arbitrary value.

trapsWithEvidence.trap: The Tailwind named colours still resolve to Electric Horizon values
trapsWithEvidence.status: LIVE — 24 sites, and invisible to the ratchet
trapsWithEvidence.evidence: theme/palette.js says so in its own header: "VALUES IN THIS FILE ARE THE ELECTRIC HORIZON PALETTE AND ARE NOT THE REDESIGN TARGET." globals.css:257 therefore declares --c-primary-500: 0 229 160. So bg-primary-500 and text-primary-600 paint NEON today. palette.js is the ratchet's single named exemption, which is exactly how this pool stayed invisible. 11 of the 24 are in app/dashboard/page-client.tsx; the rest are in components/ui/{Stepper,Avatar,DataTable,Progress,Tabs}.tsx and app/dashboard/analytics/page-client.tsx.
trapsWithEvidence.forTheCodemod: See paletteRepointFeasibility. Convert the 24 first, re-point after. Also widen the ratchet regex to cover primary|eh — or they stay invisible.

trapsWithEvidence.trap: black and white utilities are not counted at all
trapsWithEvidence.status: LIVE — 172 sites, 45 of them carrying an opacity modifier
trapsWithEvidence.evidence: Measured over the ratchet corpus: text-white 111, bg-black/50 18, text-white/80 6, bg-white 6, border-white/10 4, border-white 3, bg-white/10 3, bg-black/70 3, bg-black 3, and a tail. The rawPaletteClasses regex lists 16 hue families and neither keyword.
trapsWithEvidence.forTheCodemod: Widen the regex and RAISE THE BASELINE BY 172 IN THE SAME COMMIT, so the ratchet stays honest instead of appearing to regress. Note bg-black/50 WORKS today (black is a real Tailwind colour with channel support) and would die if rewritten to bg-[var(--scrim)]/50 — so --scrim must either carry its own alpha, like --surface-glass and --c-eh-card do, or be registered as a channel-backed named colour.

trapsWithEvidence.trap: Mapping a fill to --primary hands it to the tenant
trapsWithEvidence.evidence: lib/customization.ts:255 sets --primary as an INLINE STYLE on <html> when a tenant has chosen a colour, which outranks every stylesheet rule. Today the 665 #00E5A0 sites paint neon regardless of tenant; after conversion to var(--primary) they all become tenant-coloured.
trapsWithEvidence.forTheCodemod: This is a BEHAVIOUR EXPANSION, not a recolour. It is what plan D3 asks for, but verify on the 3-tenant matrix PER BATCH, not once at the end. Focus rings are the case to get right: map ring-[#00E5A0] to --focus-ring-color (which is var(--primary-ink), contrast-derived per tenant), NEVER to --primary — a raw tenant fill can be 1.6:1.

frozenLandmine.severity: HIGHEST — this is the one that breaks production
frozenLandmine.why: These are DATA WRITTEN TO THE TENANT RECORD and the CHOICES OFFERED to the tenant, not chrome. They must stay byte-identical to each other AND to what middleware getBranding() synthesises (organizations.service.ts, whose comment already requires it).
frozenLandmine.failureMode: Rewriting them breaks isUnbrandedDefault() at lib/customization.ts:196, whose failure mode is --primary force-set to neon as an inline style on <html> FOR EVERY TENANT, beating the entire Little Worlds palette. That is the exact bug commit c6d44695 just fixed: measured live, .eh-btn-neon painted its --lw-on-forest label at 1.43:1 where the token pairing promises 9.70:1.
frozenLandmine.instruction: The codemod must have these five locations on a hard deny-list, not merely be expected to skip them.

darkPanelDecision._: SETTLED 2026-09-18 by the lead, after the owner delegated it. This is the rule the B2 batch follows; it is not a per-file judgement call.
darkPanelDecision.rule: Vizora's own CHROME goes light. Anything that FRAMES CUSTOMER MEDIA stays dark, deliberately, as a viewport.
darkPanelDecision.why: The two groups were lumped together because they share hex values, but they do different jobs. A dark slab beside a light login form is leftover Electric Horizon substrate with no reason to be dark once the product is light. A dark surround around a playlist preview is doing real work: it is a letterbox, the same reason video players and image lightboxes are dark. A light surround tints how the customer perceives their own media, so going light there would be a functional regression dressed as consistency.

goesLight.note: SupportRequestDetail is already done (b7f4b768) and is the worked example: it was app chrome, it went light, and doing so fixed a 1.77:1 contrast failure. ValuePanel/MiniDashboard follow in W1 - and W1 must ALSO remove the false claims living there ('Join 2,500+ organizations', and the AI/256-bit/99.9% copy on the auth surfaces), which the homepage handoff flagged and which are still shipping.

staysDark.note: Stays dark, but NOT as scattered hex literals. Introduce explicit viewport tokens (--viewport-bg / --viewport-surface / --viewport-border) so the darkness is a recorded decision rather than debt the next pass tries to 'fix'. The ratchet should then see these files as converted, not excluded.
staysDark.displayClientCaveat: app/display/* is the TV client. It stays dark for a product reason beyond letterboxing: these screens idle overnight in venues, and a full-screen white rectangle at 3am in a dark room is a customer-visible problem, not a style choice. Treat as frozen.

darkPanelDecision.propagation: Any future panel inherits by asking one question: is it showing Vizora, or is it showing the customer's content? Vizora -> light. Customer content -> viewport dark.
